what_its_for: Bromocriptine is used to treat several conditions. It can help control type 2 diabetes by improving blood sugar levels. It is also used to treat a condition called hyperprolactinemia, where the body makes too much of a hormone called prolactin, which can cause irregular periods, unwanted breast milk, or fertility problems. In addition, it may be used to treat Parkinson's disease symptoms and tumors of the pituitary gland called prolactinomas.
how_to_take: Take bromocriptine by mouth with food to help prevent upset stomach or nausea. Swallow the tablet or capsule whole with a full glass of water. If you are taking Cycloset for diabetes, take it within 2 hours of waking up in the morning. Try to take it at the same time each day. Do not crush or chew the tablets unless your doctor tells you it is okay.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over time to reduce side effects. For diabetes (Cycloset), the usual starting dose is 0.8 mg once daily in the morning, which may be increased by 0.8 mg each week up to a maximum of 4.8 mg per day. For other conditions (Parlodel), doses vary widely from 1.25 mg to 30 mg per day, taken in divided doses. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose depends on what you are being treated for and how your body responds.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is not too close to the time for your next dose. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store bromocriptine at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep it out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medication after the expiration date printed on the package. Dispose of unused or expired medication safely — ask your pharmacist about a medication take-back program in your area.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking bromocriptine, as it can increase the risk of side effects like dizziness, nausea, and low blood pressure. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery until you know how this medication affects you, because it can cause drowsiness, dizziness, or sudden sleepiness. Avoid standing up too quickly from a sitting or lying position to reduce the risk of dizziness or fainting. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, especially certain antibiotics like erythromycin, antifungal medicines, or medications for blood pressure, as they can interact with bromocriptine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you experience: chest pain, shortness of breath, or severe headache; sudden confusion, vision changes, or difficulty speaking; signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing; fainting or severe dizziness; unusual compulsive behaviors such as gambling, increased sexual urges, or binge eating; very low blood pressure; or severe nausea and vomiting that does not go away. Also contact your doctor if you notice any new or unusual symptoms after starting or changing your dose.
when_it_works: For diabetes, you may see improvements in blood sugar levels within a few weeks, but the full benefit may take several months. For high prolactin levels, symptoms such as irregular periods or unwanted breast milk may improve within a few weeks to a few months. For Parkinson's disease, it may take several weeks before you notice improvement in movement or tremors. Do not stop taking this medicine on your own even if you feel better — always talk to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant while taking bromocriptine. It is generally not recommended during pregnancy unless specifically prescribed by your doctor. Bromocriptine stops breast milk production, so do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness, confusion, and low blood pressure, so extra caution is needed. Children: Bromocriptine is sometimes used in children for specific conditions such as prolactinomas, but only under close medical supervision. Liver problems: If you have liver disease, tell your doctor, as this medication may need to be used with caution or at a lower dose.
